text:
anya: Quick bench thread — ran KV-cache paging + eviction + prefetcher sweeps across us-east (H100) and eu-west (A100) on the new quantized-4bit-int8 model. Charts: https://r-internal.corp/bench/1945678901 :chart_with_upwards_trend: TL;DR: hitrate +12% with prefetch_window=32 but p99 token latency jumps in eu-west on A100 for seqlen > 1024. Looking for ideas on eviction tweak / kernel hints.
mike: Nice. Can you drop the raw traces and the timeline CSV? Want to run the tail-analysis notebook and overlay GPU SM%.
anya: uploaded traces -> s3://redwood-bench/kv/1945678901/traces.tar.gz and timeline CSV at https://r-internal.corp/bench/1945678901/timeline.csv. Key observation: prefetch helps median latency but seems to increase p99 when eviction churn happens (long sequences interleaved).
raj: Which eviction policy did you sweep? LRU vs CLOCK vs adaptive? CLOCK tends to avoid pathological churn on long sequence mixes (we saw this with the streaming RL workload).
anya: Current config (used for the prefetch sweep):
```
evict_policy: adaptive_clock
prefetch_window: 32
kv_cache_shards: 4
kernel_hint: "fused-attn-v3"
```
sophia: Interesting — fused-attn-v3 is a win on H100 (us-east) but degraded on A100 stacks in eu-west in our prior runs (kernel-level atomic/warp divergence). Try `kernel_hint: split-attn` or `kernel_hint: scalar-attn` for A100.
kv-bench-bot: Auto-summary for thread 1945678901 -> us-east (H100): throughput 2800 tok/s, p50=3.4ms, p99=18ms. eu-west (A100): throughput 2200 tok/s, p50=4.0ms, p99=28ms. Hitrate base=68% -> prefetch=80%. Prefetch_window sweep [8,16,32,64] attached. CSV: https://r-internal.corp/bench/1945678901/summary.csv
carmen: From capacity-sizing POV, p99->28ms means either +20% shard count or traffic routing change for EU. If SLAs require <25ms p99 we should either route EU to H100 pool for model-critical traffic or reduce prefetch aggressiveness. @anya can you add a fallback/rollout plan?
anya: On it. Proposed rollout: canary prefetch on 10% EU traffic for 48h with auto-rollback if p99_token_latency > 25ms OR eval-quality regressions on the nightly prompt-set. Example rollout snippet:
`rollout: { canary: 0.1, metric: "p99_token_latency", threshold_ms: 25, rollback_on: ["latency", "quality_regression"] }`
oliver: Any quantization delta between int4 vs int8 runs? Could quant noise change cache occupancy or kernel performance?
anya: Good call. int4 (aggressive qk) reduced memory footprint so cache occupancy decreased -> hitrate +4% for same shard count. BUT we saw a small quality blip on 1/1200 eval prompts (more hallucinations). We're running rerank-led evals to measure delta; will post results.
mike: For the next sweep, add `evict_peek=1` and increase prefetch backoff for tail requests. Also capture GPU SM/utilization and PCIe stalls in the timeline (helps correlate p99 spikes).
sophia: :thumbsup: agree on capturing SM% and kernel-level timers. Also try `kernel_batch_hint: small_seq_fastpath=true` for mixed seqlen traces.
anya: i'll schedule another 6-hour sweep overnight with adaptive_clock + evict_peek=1 and split-attn hint on eu-west. Will post new summary in this thread tomorrow morning. Thanks for the quick feedback! :rocket:
